plan: With a private value of $6, my goal is to maximize potential profit while minimizing risk. Since the prize is worth $6 to me, I want to bid strategically. A bid too low risks losing the item, while a bid too high risks negative earnings. Given the first-price sealed bid auction mechanism where I pay the second-highest bid, I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances while protecting downside.

My private value is $40. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. The worst case with a $40 bid is paying slightly less than $40 if another bidder also bids near my value, which still preserves most of my potential profit.
